summary: Retained Fidelity capacity head #419 validates PolicyInputs as a metatable-free table and validates all seven recognized values, but it never closes the runtime input record against unknown keys. Extra string or non-string keys are silently ignored by evaluatePolicy()/step(). This is the same fail-closed record-shape class as the already-proposed HG-FIDELITY-CONFIG-CLOSED-SHAPE defect, so fold PolicyInputs closure into that leaf instead of opening competing FidelityManager source/test WIP. An otherwise-valid input record carrying a misspelled directlyObserved/visible/relevance field should reject deterministically before policy evaluation, while all exactly-shaped under-contract inputs preserve existing F0-F4 semantics and no-execute behavior.
evidence: Retained Fidelity capacity PR #419 exact head 1f017628bf49365663dfc2db3a30b81ba477a0a3 defines PolicyInputs with exactly seven fields: distanceStuds, visible, directlyObserved, secondsSinceInteraction, significance, networkRelevance, and entityRelevance.

At that exact head, validateInputs() checks type(inputs) == table, rejects a metatable, then dereferences and validates only those seven recognized fields. It never enumerates supplied keys or compares them against a fixed schema, so extra keys survive validation and are ignored by evaluatePolicy().

The retained tests/fidelity_manager.luau inputs(overrides) helper writes arbitrary override keys into an otherwise-valid input table. Existing tests exercise value-domain and metatable rejection but contain no unknown-key rejection case, so an override typo can remain observationally silent.

Concrete semantic case: an otherwise-valid record with directlyObserved=false plus misspelled directlyObseved=true is accepted; the intended observation signal is discarded and policy evaluates using false. The same applies to misspelled visibility/relevance fields. Fail-closed rejection is preferable at this typed runtime contract boundary.

Repository PR and live lane search found no separate Fidelity PolicyInputs closed-shape repair. HG-FIDELITY-CONFIG-CLOSED-SHAPE already owns the same source/tests and the same unknown-record-key defect class for PolicyConfig, so expanding that one PROPOSED leaf avoids duplicate WIP.
No local Luau/Lune execution, Roblox Studio, device-performance measurement, viewport, physical-contact, or two-client evidence is claimed by this mining result.
